unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Fenbrook Organic Dairy is a partnership owned by Rachel and Tom Ellery in the rural market town of Fenwick Dale for 9 years. The dairy has 180 cows, pasteurises milk on-site and employs 22 staff. Last year it generated $680,000 in revenue, selling milk and yoghurt to 14 shops across the county.

Green demand is growing: retailers report organic dairy sales up 25% this year, and a national supermarket chain has offered Fenbrook a $240,000 annual contract if the dairy gains accredited organic certification. Certification requires a 2-year conversion plus a $90,000 audit and fencing package. The partners could instead use the $90,000 to double yoghurt capacity and extend their own-label range. They are unsure whether the higher sales justify the disruption and must decide within the next month.

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Brackenford Dye Works is a private limited company that dyes cotton fabrics for garment makers in Country X for 17 years, employing 95 workers near the River Arn. The plant uses 60,000 litres of water a day, and last year revenue was $4,300,000.

New legal controls cap dye-house chemical discharge at 0.8 milligrams per litre from January. A recent test found Brackenford discharging 1.5 milligrams per litre, exposing the firm to fines of $5,000 per day. The company could install a $720,000 water treatment plant, or request a 6-month extension while continuing to pay fines. Two buyers worth $1,100,000 a year have warned they will switch suppliers if the discharge limit is breached. Local residents have complained for years about coloured foam in the river.

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity

It produces 900 tonnes of fish a year, supplying frozen fillets to food processors, and last year revenue was $3,600,000. It is the largest fish farm in the region.

Retailers now demand certified sustainable fish. Brinewater can switch to certified feed and remove antibiotic growth promoters for an extra $480,000 a year. Keeping the cheaper feed would protect profits but risks losing two supermarket chains worth $1,500,000 a year. An animal welfare group has published claims that the current feed included routine antibiotics, which Brinewater denies. A survey of 2,400 shoppers found 68% prefer stores with plastic-free packaging. Thornwick could invest $360,000 in reusable crates and paper alternatives to keep all 11 stores compliant, or switch to thinner recycled plastic at a saving of $210,000 in year one, which may not meet the new rules. unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Brinsworth Timber Co is a partnership importing hardwood and softwood for two furniture factories in Country X for 11 years, employing 73 workers across import, storage and delivery. Revenue last year was $6,800,000 from 9 major customers.

Demand for certified wood from Country X furniture makers has grown quickly, and retailers advertise certified furniture as a selling point. The country's largest furniture retailer, worth $2,600,000 a year to Brinsworth, now requires all timber to carry independently certified sustainable forestry labels. Certified timber costs 16% more, adding about $540,000 a year to input costs. A cheaper uncertified supplier offers timber at the old price, but its origin documents are unclear. unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Hollowgate Recycling Co is a private limited company sorting commercial waste in Country X for 10 years, employing 66 staff. Revenue last year was $2,750,000. It collects from offices, factories and shops across three provinces and sorts cardboard, plastics and metals.

The government landfill tax rises from $88 to $130 per tonne in April. Hollowgate sent 5,200 tonnes of residual waste to landfill last year, so its tax bill would rise from $457,600 to $676,000 a year. The company could invest $700,000 in an automated sorting line that would cut landfill waste by 60%, saving about $405,600 a year in tax, or continue as it is and pass the extra $218,400 on to customers. The board has 4 months to decide.
